name: Landlord registration deadline and evidence tracker
demand: England had 5.03 million private-rented dwellings at 31 March 2025; this is a market-size proxy, not an exact count of properties covered by the new rules (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/dwelling-stock-estimates-in-england-2025/dwelling-stock-estimates-england-31-march-2025). The English Private Landlord Survey reports 4.7 million private-renting households in 2023–24 (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report/english-private-landlord-survey-2024-main-report), and a Commons committee report cites about 2.3 million landlords in England (https://publications.parliament.uk/pa/cm5902/cmselect/cmcomloc/42/report.html). Separately, HMRC counted 2.88 million UK unincorporated landlords reporting rental income in 2024–25; that is UK-wide and excludes incorporated landlords and some people below Self Assessment reporting thresholds (https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/property-rental-income-statistics/property-rental-income-statistics-2026). Google Play shows 10k+ downloads for Lendlord’s general landlord app, not for its new registration feature or as a count of active users (https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=lendlord.lendlord). Search volume, active users and paid demand for this specific tracker are unverified.
prices: The government service charges £65 per property per year, with annual renewal; the official service itself supplies registration and compliance evidence (https://housinghub.campaign.gov.uk/renting-is-changing/get-ready-to-register/). Lendlord’s exact registration-preparation feature is free in its Compliance Hub; its broader plans list free, £12/month and £36/month tiers (https://lendlord.io/solutions/manage/property-register/; https://lendlord.io/uk-plan/). NRLA offers a free postcode deadline checker (https://www.nrla.org.uk/resources/renters-rights/landlord-database-register-your-rental-property-service). Adjacent tenancy-management software advertises a free single-property tier and paid plans from £7.99/month (https://letcompliance.com/pricing). Letkept lists £8 per property/month for a planned product but is collecting waitlist signups; this is an asking price, not evidence of completed sales (https://letkept.co.uk/).

revenue_proof.claim: Revenue from this tracker feature is unverified. Lendlord publishes plan prices and feature descriptions, but no dated sales or payment data for the feature.

copy_speed: The cheap kill-check missed a direct competitor: Lendlord announced its Property Register tool on 13 October 2026. It prepares registration packs, flags missing details, tracks regional deadlines, and handles renewal reminders; the feature is free in its Compliance Hub (https://www.cherryplc.co.uk/industry/pressreleases/details/24782; https://lendlord.io/solutions/manage/property-register/). NRLA has a free deadline checker, and Quarterday publicly offers a free postcode checker; their launch dates are unverified (https://www.nrla.org.uk/resources/renters-rights/landlord-database-register-your-rental-property-service; https://getquarterday.co.uk/). Letkept advertises a similar evidence pack and reminders but says it is not open yet; its launch date is unverified (https://letkept.co.uk/).
platform_risk: High. The official GOV.UK service is mandatory, charges the statutory fee, asks for landlord/property/safety information, and says registration lets landlords demonstrate compliance; it also offers guidance and a contact centre (https://housinghub.campaign.gov.uk/renting-is-changing/get-ready-to-register/). Landlords must start registration themselves; agents may provide certain information on their behalf (same source). The official guidance reviewed does not state a third-party API or partner integration. A third-party product therefore appears to be a preparation layer around a government-owned process, which could change its fields or guidance.
defensible_asset: Weak for a standalone tracker. The rules, deadlines and required fields are published by government, and an established competitor already offers the same registration-preparation workflow for free (https://housinghub.campaign.gov.uk/renting-is-changing/get-ready-to-register/; https://lendlord.io/solutions/manage/property-register/). Inference: a maintained, source-linked rules engine and a record of documents, reminders and changes could create some practical value, but the government service remains the registration record and the user’s data can be re-entered elsewhere. A broader, trusted compliance history across landlord obligations would be more defensible than deadline tracking alone.
build_effort: A narrow self-serve product would need postcode-to-region deadlines, landlord/property checklists, certificate uploads, OCR with user confirmation, evidence export, renewal/change reminders and a dated rules source log. The government lists personal details and gas, electrical and EPC information among the inputs, so secure handling and deletion/export controls are core requirements (https://housinghub.campaign.gov.uk/renting-is-changing/get-ready-to-register/). Keep deadline calculations deterministic; use agents for draft rule monitoring, document extraction, reminder operations and support triage, with human review before legal-rule changes ship. Actual build effort and operating workload are unverified. The 60% automation figure below is a design hypothesis, not a measured result.
channel: Use search-led content, a free postcode deadline checker, paid search experiments and opt-in reminders or partner referrals. Do not use cold email, SMS, WhatsApp or DMs to individual landlords or sole traders: ICO guidance treats sole traders as individual subscribers and generally requires prior consent or a valid soft opt-in for electronic-mail marketing (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/business-to-business-marketing/).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; ≤5 hours/week is a target to measure in a paid pilot, not an established operating result. Annual renewals and changing rules still create ongoing support and review work (https://housinghub.campaign.gov.uk/renting-is-changing/get-ready-to-register/).
desk_test: Within one day, make a one-page mockup for the potentially differentiated part—multi-property evidence preparation and change/renewal history, not just deadline lookup. Offer a sample evidence pack and a refundable preorder at £8/property/month, explicitly treating Letkept’s listed price as a test anchor rather than proven market pricing (https://letkept.co.uk/). Share it only through moderator-approved public landlord communities or opt-in channels. Count paid commitments, not free email signups, as the signal; if nobody pays, do not build a standalone tracker.
red_flags: The claimed survivor verdict should be revised: a direct, free competing registration tool was announced on 13 October 2026, and free deadline checkers also exist (https://www.cherryplc.co.uk/industry/pressreleases/details/24782; https://www.nrla.org.uk/resources/renters-rights/landlord-database-register-your-rental-property-service). The government service itself supplies the registration and evidence function, so willingness to pay for a separate tracker is unproven (https://housinghub.campaign.gov.uk/renting-is-changing/get-ready-to-register/). No verified revenue event for this product was found; published prices are not proof of payment. Search volume, product-specific installs, automation share and ≤5-hour owner workload remain unverified. Treat the narrow idea as killed unless the paid desk test validates a broader evidence workflow.
